caveats:
AI predictions. Cross-sensor pre and post plus post-cloud can inflate destroyed calls.
Coverage limited to the current post-imagery footprint. Field verification is the ground truth.

Evaluated and validated against 3,896 OSM manually tagged affected buildings (3,185 destroyed
+ 711 damaged, 2026-09-11): destroyed precision 0.91, recall 0.78, F1 0.84; severe (major +
destroyed) recall against manually tagged affected buildings 0.75.
name: hot_flood_npl_buildings_damage
notes:
Part of the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team response activation for the 26 August 2026 Bhote Koshi and Trishuli flash flood in Nepal. AI-scored building damage per OpenStreetMap footprint across the upper Trishuli and Bhote Koshi corridor, from Rasuwagadhi to the Narayani confluence. Post imagery is a 26-scene Vantor open-data composite (2026-08-27 to 2026-09-08, roughly 0.4 m/px, about 9.8% cloud). Pre imagery is ESRI World Imagery. Building footprints come from OpenStreetMap and cover 20,367 features in the corridor; 9,748 fall inside the current post-imagery footprint and carry an AI damage class. Each feature carries `osm_id`, `osm_type`, `building`, a `damage` label (`no-visible-damage`, `minor-damage`, `major-damage`, `destroyed`, `no-data`) and a `damage_confidence`. Evaluated and validated against 3,896 OSM manually tagged affected buildings (3,185 destroyed + 711 damaged, 2026-09-11): destroyed precision 0.91, recall 0.78, F1 0.84; severe (major + destroyed) recall against manually tagged affected buildings 0.75. The reference layer is included in this dataset. Post-event imagery TMS: 
https://titiler.hotosm.org/cog/tiles/WebMercatorQuad/{z}/{x}/{y}?url=https://production-raw-data-api.s3.amazonaws.com/ISO3/NPL/buildings/hot_flood_npl_buildings_damage_post.tif
For the wider corridor context, see [Nepal Flood 2026 Flood Affected Area](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/hot_flood_npl). - Source: [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/), Vantor open data, ESRI World Imagery - Part of HOT disaster response exports on HDX by [HOT](https://www.hotosm.org/)

Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team (HOT) acts as a bridge between the traditional humanitarian responders and the OpenStreetMap Community. HOT works both remotely and physically in countries to assist the collection of geographic data, usage of that information and training others in OpenStreetMap.
